newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares stumble lower at volatile close.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares stumble lower at volatile close.

text.p: Singapore shares stumbled lower at the close of trade on Thursday after a volatile session led mostly by high turnover in Malaysian issues, dealers said.
Early jitters over Wednesday's remarks by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, warning short-term interest rates could rise to check inflation, was largely dismissed.
"It was a factor in peoples' decision-making but not the reason for the late selling," a dealer with a local bank said.
The Straits Times Industrials Index skidded 25.44 points to 2,190.63 at the close on a volume of 430.8 million shares.
Malaysian over-the-counter (OTC) stocks, which recovered in early action, were extremely volatile as they were hit by a combination of speculative selling and short covering.
"It came down on settlement rumours, but there was no confirmation of this," one remisier said, referring to rumours about changes to the settlement period.
Malaysian stocks dominated actives with IGB Corp hitting new highs at Singapore S1.09, and settling up $0.20 to S$1.03.
Losers comprised a broad cross-section of blue chips. City Dev warrants fell S$0.50 to S$11.60 and SPH foreign eased S$0.40 to S$27.30.
